How to redirect a deceased person's mail (Australia Post)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 2 Nov 2026

Australia Post offers up to 12 months of free mail redirection for a deceased estate. The executor or administrator, or someone legally entitled to deal with the estate, applies in person at any Post Office with a completed mail redirection form, their proof of identity, and an original or certified copy of a document proving their entitlement, such as the grant of probate, letters of administration or the will naming them executor.

Key facts

  • Up to 12 months free for deceased estates
  • Apply in person at any Post Office
  • Needs the form, your ID and proof of entitlement
  • Originals or certified copies only

What are the steps?

  1. Get a mail redirection form: download Australia Post's PDF or pick up a printed one at the Post Office.
  2. Gather your proof of identity.
  3. Gather proof that you're entitled to deal with the estate, as an original or certified copy of one of these: the grant of probate naming you executor; letters of administration naming you administrator; the death certificate plus an original statutory declaration of your relationship and entitlement; the will naming you executor; or an original statutory declaration giving the deceased's full name, date of death, address and your relationship and entitlement.
  4. Apply in person at any Post Office in Australia. Australia Post says deceased-estate redirections are applied for in person.
  5. Redirect to an address you check often. Bank statements, bills, renewal notices and subscription letters help you find accounts and recurring payments to close, including digital ones.
  6. Need longer than 12 months? Australia Post says its usual rates apply after the free period.
  7. Use the redirected mail to build your list of who to notify, and see our guides to banks, super, telcos and government services.

Frequently asked questions

Is mail redirection free for a deceased estate?

Yes, for up to 12 months. Australia Post says executors or administrators of an estate may be eligible for free redirection, with normal rates after that.

Can I redirect a deceased person's mail online?

Australia Post's special circumstances page says to apply in person at any Post Office, with the form, your ID and proof of entitlement.

Do I need probate to redirect mail?

Not necessarily. Australia Post also accepts the will naming you executor, or the death certificate with a statutory declaration, or a statutory declaration with the required details. Originals or certified copies only.

What should the statutory declaration say?

Australia Post lists the deceased's full name and date of death, the address mail is redirected from, your relationship to the deceased, and that you're legally entitled to deal with the estate.

Why redirect a deceased person's mail?

Letters reveal accounts, bills and subscriptions the family may not know about, and stop mail piling up at an empty home.
